styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wooden shelf cabinet with rows of dolls. Its measured facts are fine: 13 colours per tile (the hedge has 10, the stall 17), 0% flat-fill coverage, and 13 colours in total, about the same as the bench and lamp. Three things still count against it. First, 68% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, more than the bench (44%), the well (33%) and the stall (1%), so the frame reads as a dark, mostly untinted outline around the whole silhouette, which is the sticker look rather than a dark wood tone. Second, 13 colours spread over the frame, shelf interiors and dolls leaves only about 3-4 lightness steps per material, against about 5-6 on the stall roof, the well roof and the hedge canopy. Third, the wood has little visible grain or highlight work, and the dolls are small, similar blobs. Next to the stall and the well it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails on the benefit of the doubt.
